Substituting "file" for "suite" does not repair that: a mutation that breaks the file's bash parsing, or that trips any other case in the same file, produces a non-zero file exit with the mutated case never failing. spec.md AC4 asks for "confirming the test goes red", singular, and the previous job's constitution had already learned this — its V-1 check reads "The exit code alone is not the check — compare the TAP `ok`/`not ok` line for each case". The load-bearing clause of this constitution dropped that.

- **B-1** (blocker): The guarded surface is defined in three clauses at three different scopes, and two of them can be satisfied while contradicting each other. B-1's text says "there is no exempt position, no exempt file", but its check globs `tests/*.bats tests/helpers.bash`, which exempts every other file under `tests/`. V-1 defines the guard's surface as "anywhere under `tests/`, covering `helpers.bash` as well as the `.bats` files". V-2 then mandates a new non-`.bats`, non-helpers file in that directory, `tests/mutation-check.sh`. A guard built to V-1's wording that flags a first-token `[[` in `mutation-check.sh` turns `bats tests/` red and fails V-3; a guard built to B-1's file list does not scan `mutation-check.sh` at all and a strict V-1 checker fails it. One clause has to own the surface, name it exactly, and say whether `tests/mutation-check.sh` is inside it.
  evidence: constitution.md:117 and :121 (B-1 text vs B-1 glob), constitution.md:156 (V-1: `anywhere under tests/`), constitution.md:177 (V-2 mandates tests/mutation-check.sh), constitution.md:192 (V-3 requires `bats tests/` to exit 0). `ls tests/` at 61213fe returns seven .bats files and nothing else, so both new files land inside the disputed region.
- **V-2** (major): The tautology probe's expected outcome depends on a mutation strategy the clause never fixes, so it will FAIL correct scripts. The checker is told to replace a converted assertion with `assert_contains ""` and "require the script to report that site as unmutable or failing". Under polarity inversion — the strategy spec.md AC4 literally names ("Verify by inverting each one") — `assert_contains ""` becomes `assert_not_contains ""`, which returns 1, so the file goes red and the script correctly reports the site mutable. The checker then fails a script that did exactly what V-2's text asked for. Needle-substitution mutation behaves the same way. "Unmutable" is also undefined: recognising an arbitrary always-true assertion is not decidable, and the clause gives no rule (e.g. "refuse to mutate an assertion with an empty needle") that a worker could build to. Either pin the mutation strategy and pick a tautology that strategy provably cannot redden, or drop the probe and get the same assurance from the case-level TAP requirement.
  evidence: constitution.md:182 (`replace one converted assertion with a tautology (for instance an assert_contains "", which matches any haystack)`) against spec.md:91 and constitution.md:177. Verified under /bin/bash 3.2.57(1): `assert_not_contains() { case "$2" in *"$1"*) return 1;; esac; }` with an empty needle returns 1 for every haystack, because `*""*` matches everything.
- **B-2** (major): One of the 54 mandated conversions is required to change and no clause checks what it changed into. B-1 requires `tests/packages.bats:146` be converted; B-2's check reads "each of the 53 converted assertions", which excludes it; V-2 excludes it by name. A worker who deletes the line outright satisfies B-1 (no first-token `[[` remains), is outside B-2's 53 pairs, is outside V-2's 53 mutations, and V-3 stays green unless the fixture happens to produce an empty cask line. The required replacement form is also stated only in the descriptive Measured baseline (`[ -n "$cask" ] || continue`), not in any clause, so a checker has no normative text to hold it to. Simplest repair: make B-2's check read 54 pairs and say what the 54th must become.

- **B-3** (major): Nothing binds a converted call site to actually call a helper, and nothing requires `helpers.bash` to define the helpers. spec.md AC1 asks that all 54 be "replaced with a helper whose failure propagates from any position ... following the assert_contains and assert_not_contains pattern".
